candidates.prompt:
A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Tantalum (탄탈럼) itself — the sovereign of the Tantalum Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: early thirties — a poised, graceful face with soft contours; at most faint lines, no deep folds or under-eye bags.
Face — her own: a cool, aloof beauty; deep brown skin; gently long oval face; medium-sized eyes — narrow upturned eyes, outer eye corners slightly lifted; thin arched brows; aquiline nose; full heart-shaped lips; teal eyes; dark berry lipstick.
Body and hair: slender-limbed yet full-busted with rounded hips and a narrow waist build; long side-swept hair with long bangs falling over one eye; dark slate blue-grey hair with a cool wet sheen, rippling like water drawing away.
Expression: a cool, knowing look.
Her element, carried in her design: tantalum: a dense, hard blue-grey metal named in 1802 for Tantalus, the king of myth punished to stand in water that drew away whenever he bent to drink, beneath fruit that lifted out of reach, because its oxide sat in strong acid without taking up any of it; nearly untouched even by aqua regia, it gave the word tantalize; for decades it was confused with its twin metal, which in 1844 was split from it and named for his daughter Niobe; the body accepts it without harm, so it makes bone implants and surgical clips; tiny tantalum capacitors hide inside phones.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

Costume: a high-fantasy royal or warrior costume — plate pauldrons or a gorget, mail or scale over a long tabard or robe, a circlet or crown, a flowing cape; metal ornament and regalia built from the traits above, subtle magical glow along the patterns.
Silhouette: a great crown and a fur-trimmed royal mantle over an ornate breastplate — a ceremonial, regal silhouette. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.
Colours: dark slate blue-grey, still teal pool water, ripe golden fruit, deep plum shadow.
Exposure (bold): her regalia opens to show skin — bare shoulders and arms between pauldron and bracer, a deep open neckline under the gorget with natural cleavage, a high slit in the tabard or robe showing the thigh; armor pieces stay on and symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: a twilight garden of the underworld: in its heart a clear, still pool whose water sinks away whenever one bends to drink, boughs heavy with ripe golden fruit that lift out of reach whenever a hand rises, a great stone hanging overhead on nothing, and beneath it a fallen king's empty golden banquet table.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: natural daylight or the world's own magical glow.

Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.
